content: Ranitidine bismuth citrate is no longer available in the United States. If you are currently taking this medication, you should contact your doctor to discuss alternative treatments. Ranitidine bismuth citrate is prescribed to treat intestinal ulcers. It works by combating infections caused by Helicobacter pylori bacteria, which are often associated with ulcers. Treating this bacterial infection helps prevent the recurrence of ulcers. This medication is used in combination with other drugs. If you have questions about additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. This medication is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically twice a day, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less than the recommended dose or take it more frequently than directed. To fully treat your ulcer, you must use this medication for at least four weeks. Continue taking it even if you feel better, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before starting ranitidine bismuth citrate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ranitidine (Zantac) or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including aspirin, antacids, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney, liver, or blood disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, let your doctor know if you have previously taken this or any other medication for ulcers. If your ulcer symptoms do not improve within the first few days of treatment, inform your doctor, as you may require a different medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Ranitidine bismuth citrate may cause mild side effects, such as temporary darkening of the tongue and stool, which are harmless. Notify your doctor if these symptoms persist or worsen. Other mild side effects may include: Headache Dizziness Changes in taste perception Constipation Stomach pain Severe side effects require immediate medical attention. Contact your doctor if you experience any of the following: Bloody, black, or tarry stools Fever Sore throat Mental confusion Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Brand names for ranitidine bismuth citrate include: Tritec® Zantac® Zantac® 75 Zantac® EFFERdose® Zantac® Premixed Zantac® Syrup
